T.d: T is a type passed to Test functions to manage test state and support formatted test logs.

T.Chdir.d: Chdir calls os.Chdir(dir) and uses Cleanup to restore the current working directory to its original value after the test.

T.Cleanup.d: Cleanup registers a function to be called when the test (or subtest) and all its subtests complete.

T.Context.d: Context returns a context that is canceled just before Cleanup-registered functions are called.

T.Deadline.d: Deadline reports the time at which the test binary will have exceeded the timeout specified by the -timeout flag.

T.Error.d: Error is equivalent to Log followed by Fail.

T.Errorf.d: Errorf is equivalent to Logf followed by Fail.

T.Fail.d: Fail marks the function as having failed but continues execution.

T.FailNow.d: FailNow marks the function as having failed and stops its execution by calling runtime.Goexit (which then runs all deferred calls in the current goroutine).

T.Failed.d: Failed reports whether the function has failed.

T.Fatal.d: Fatal is equivalent to Log followed by FailNow.

T.Fatalf.d: Fatalf is equivalent to Logf followed by FailNow.

T.Helper.d: Helper marks the calling function as a test helper function.

T.Log.d: Log formats its arguments using default formatting, analogous to Println, and records the text in the error log.

T.Logf.d: Logf formats its arguments according to the format, analogous to Printf, and records the text in the error log.

T.Name.d: Name returns the name of the running (sub-) test or benchmark.

T.Parallel.d: Parallel signals that this test is to be run in parallel with (and only with) other parallel tests.

T.Run.s: func (t *T) Run(name string, f func(t *T)) bool
T.Run.d: Run runs f as a subtest of t called name.

T.Setenv.d: Setenv calls os.Setenv(key, value) and uses Cleanup to restore the environment variable to its original value after the test.

T.Skip.d: Skip is equivalent to Log followed by SkipNow.

T.SkipNow.d: SkipNow marks the test as having been skipped and stops its execution by calling runtime.Goexit.

T.Skipf.d: Skipf is equivalent to Logf followed by SkipNow.

T.Skipped.d: Skipped reports whether the test was skipped.

T.TempDir.d: TempDir returns a temporary directory for the test to use.

Duration.d: A Duration represents the elapsed time between two instants as an int64 nanosecond count.

Duration.Abs.d: Abs returns the absolute value of d.

Duration.Hours.d: Hours returns the duration as a floating point number of hours.

Duration.Microseconds.d: Microseconds returns the duration as an integer microsecond count.

Duration.Milliseconds.d: Milliseconds returns the duration as an integer millisecond count.

Duration.Minutes.d: Minutes returns the duration as a floating point number of minutes.

Duration.Nanoseconds.d: Nanoseconds returns the duration as an integer nanosecond count.

Duration.Round.d: Round returns the result of rounding d to the nearest multiple of m.

Duration.Seconds.d: Seconds returns the duration as a floating point number of seconds.

Duration.String.d: String returns a string representing the duration in the form "72h3m0.5s".

Duration.Truncate.d: Truncate returns the result of rounding d toward zero to a multiple of m.

FixedZone.d: FixedZone returns a Location that always uses the given zone name and offset (seconds east of UTC).

Kitchen.d: These are predefined layouts for use in Time.Format and time.Parse.

Layout.d: These are predefined layouts for use in Time.Format and time.Parse.

LoadLocation.d: LoadLocation returns the Location with the given name.

LoadLocationFromTZData.d: LoadLocationFromTZData returns a Location with the given name initialized from the IANA Time Zone database-formatted data.

Local.d: Local represents the system's local time zone.

Location.d: A Location maps time instants to the zone in use at that time.

Location.String.d: String returns a descriptive name for the time zone information, corresponding to the name argument to LoadLocation or FixedZone.

Month.d: A Month specifies a month of the year (January = 1, ...).

Month.String.d: String returns the English name of the month ("January", "February", ...).

NewTicker.d: NewTicker returns a new Ticker containing a channel that will send the current time on the channel after each tick.

NewTimer.d: NewTimer creates a new Timer that will send the current time on its channel after at least duration d.

Now.d: Now returns the current local time.

Parse.d: Parse parses a formatted string and returns the time value it represents.

ParseError.d: ParseError describes a problem parsing a time string.

RubyDate.d: These are predefined layouts for use in Time.Format and time.Parse.

Since.d: Since returns the time elapsed since t.

Sleep.d: Sleep pauses the current goroutine for at least the duration d.

Stamp.d: These are predefined layouts for use in Time.Format and time.Parse.

StampMicro.d: These are predefined layouts for use in Time.Format and time.Parse.

StampMilli.d: These are predefined layouts for use in Time.Format and time.Parse.

StampNano.d: These are predefined layouts for use in Time.Format and time.Parse.

Ticker.d: A Ticker holds a channel that delivers “ticks” of a clock at intervals.

Ticker.Reset.d: Reset stops a ticker and resets its period to the specified duration.

Time.s: Time struct { // contains filtered or unexported fields }
Time.d: A Time represents an instant in time with nanosecond precision.

Time.AddDate.s: func (t Time) AddDate(years int, months int, days int) Time
Time.AddDate.d: AddDate returns the time corresponding to adding the given number of years, months, and days to t.

Time.After.d: After reports whether the time instant t is after u.

Time.AppendFormat.d: AppendFormat is like Time.Format but appends the textual representation to b and returns the extended buffer.

Time.Before.d: Before reports whether the time instant t is before u.

Time.Clock.s: func (t Time) Clock() (hour, min, sec int)
Time.Clock.d: Clock returns the hour, minute, and second within the day specified by t.

Time.Compare.d: Compare compares the time instant t with u.

Time.Date.s: func (t Time) Date() (year int, month Month, day int)
Time.Date.d: Date returns the year, month, and day in which t occurs.

Time.Day.d: Day returns the day of the month specified by t.

Time.Equal.d: Equal reports whether t and u represent the same time instant.

Time.Format.d: Format returns a textual representation of the time value formatted according to the layout defined by the argument.

Time.GoString.d: GoString implements fmt.GoStringer and formats t to be printed in Go source code.

Time.Hour.d: Hour returns the hour within the day specified by t, in the range [0, 23].

Time.ISOWeek.d: ISOWeek returns the ISO 8601 year and week number in which t occurs.

Time.In.d: In returns a copy of t representing the same time instant, but with the copy's location information set to loc for display purposes.

Time.IsDST.d: IsDST reports whether the time in the configured location is in Daylight Savings Time.

Time.IsZero.d: IsZero reports whether t represents the zero time instant, January 1, year 1, 00:00:00 UTC.

Time.Local.d: Local returns t with the location set to local time.

Time.Location.d: Location returns the time zone information associated with t.

Time.Minute.d: Minute returns the minute offset within the hour specified by t, in the range [0, 59].

Time.Month.d: Month returns the month of the year specified by t.

Time.Nanosecond.d: Nanosecond returns the nanosecond offset within the second specified by t, in the range [0, 999999999].

Time.Round.d: Round returns the result of rounding t to the nearest multiple of d (since the zero time).

Time.Second.d: Second returns the second offset within the minute specified by t, in the range [0, 59].

Time.String.d: String returns the time formatted using the format string "2006-01-02 15:04:05.999999999 -0700 MST" If the time has a monotonic clock reading, the returned string includes a final field "m=±<value>", where value is the monotonic clock r…

Time.Truncate.d: Truncate returns the result of rounding t down to a multiple of d (since the zero time).

Time.UTC.d: UTC returns t with the location set to UTC.

Time.Unix.d: Unix returns t as a Unix time, the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC.

Time.UnixMicro.d: UnixMicro returns t as a Unix time, the number of microseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC.

Time.UnixMilli.d: UnixMilli returns t as a Unix time, the number of milliseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC.

Time.UnixNano.d: UnixNano returns t as a Unix time, the number of nanoseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC.

Time.Weekday.d: Weekday returns the day of the week specified by t.

Time.Year.d: Year returns the year in which t occurs.

Time.YearDay.d: YearDay returns the day of the year specified by t, in the range [1,365] for non-leap years, and [1,366] in leap years.

Time.Zone.s: func (t Time) Zone() (name string, offset int)
Time.Zone.d: Zone computes the time zone in effect at time t, returning the abbreviated name of the zone (such as "CET") and its offset in seconds east of UTC.

Time.ZoneBounds.d: ZoneBounds returns the bounds of the time zone in effect at time t.

Timer.d: The Timer type represents a single event.

Timer.Reset.d: Reset changes the timer to expire after duration d.

Timer.Stop.d: Stop prevents the Timer from firing.

Unix.s: func Unix(sec int64, nsec int64) Time
Unix.d: Unix returns the local Time corresponding to the given Unix time, sec seconds and nsec nanoseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

UnixDate.d: These are predefined layouts for use in Time.Format and time.Parse.

UnixMicro.d: UnixMicro returns the local Time corresponding to the given Unix time, usec microseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

UnixMilli.d: UnixMilli returns the local Time corresponding to the given Unix time, msec milliseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.

Until.d: Until returns the duration until t.

Weekday.d: A Weekday specifies a day of the week (Sunday = 0, ...).

Weekday.String.d: String returns the English name of the day ("Sunday", "Monday", ...).

CaseRange.s: CaseRange struct { Lo uint32 Hi uint32 Delta d }
CaseRange.d: CaseRange represents a range of Unicode code points for simple (one code point to one code point) case conversion.

CaseRanges.d: CaseRanges is the table describing case mappings for all letters with non-self mappings.

Categories.d: Categories is the set of Unicode category tables.

FoldCategory.d: FoldCategory maps a category name to a table of code points outside the category that are equivalent under simple case folding to code points inside the category.

FoldScript.d: FoldScript maps a script name to a table of code points outside the script that are equivalent under simple case folding to code points inside the script.

GraphicRanges.d: GraphicRanges defines the set of graphic characters according to Unicode.

In.d: In reports whether the rune is a member of one of the ranges.

Is.d: Is reports whether the rune is in the specified table of ranges.

IsControl.d: IsControl reports whether the rune is a control character.

IsDigit.d: IsDigit reports whether the rune is a decimal digit.

IsGraphic.d: IsGraphic reports whether the rune is defined as a Graphic by Unicode.

IsLetter.d: IsLetter reports whether the rune is a letter (category L).

IsLower.d: IsLower reports whether the rune is a lower case letter.

IsMark.d: IsMark reports whether the rune is a mark character (category M).

IsNumber.d: IsNumber reports whether the rune is a number (category N).

IsOneOf.d: IsOneOf reports whether the rune is a member of one of the ranges.

IsPrint.d: IsPrint reports whether the rune is defined as printable by Go.

IsPunct.d: IsPunct reports whether the rune is a Unicode punctuation character (category P).

IsSpace.d: IsSpace reports whether the rune is a space character as defined by Unicode's White Space property; in the Latin-1 space this is '\t', '\n', '\v', '\f', '\r', ' ', U+0085 (NEL), U+00A0 (NBSP).

IsSymbol.d: IsSymbol reports whether the rune is a symbolic character.

IsTitle.d: IsTitle reports whether the rune is a title case letter.

IsUpper.d: IsUpper reports whether the rune is an upper case letter.

LowerCase.d: Indices into the Delta arrays inside CaseRanges for case mapping.

MaxCase.d: Indices into the Delta arrays inside CaseRanges for case mapping.

PrintRanges.d: PrintRanges defines the set of printable characters according to Go.

Properties.d: Properties is the set of Unicode property tables.

Range16.s: Range16 struct { Lo uint16 Hi uint16 Stride uint16 }
Range16.d: Range16 represents of a range of 16-bit Unicode code points.

Range32.s: Range32 struct { Lo uint32 Hi uint32 Stride uint32 }
Range32.d: Range32 represents of a range of Unicode code points and is used when one or more of the values will not fit in 16 bits.

RangeTable.s: RangeTable struct { R16 []Range16 R32 []Range32 LatinOffset int // number of entries in R16 with Hi <= MaxLatin1 }
RangeTable.d: RangeTable defines a set of Unicode code points by listing the ranges of code points within the set.

Scripts.d: Scripts is the set of Unicode script tables.

SimpleFold.d: SimpleFold iterates over Unicode code points equivalent under the Unicode-defined simple case folding.

SpecialCase.d: SpecialCase represents language-specific case mappings such as Turkish.

SpecialCase.ToLower.d: ToLower maps the rune to lower case giving priority to the special mapping.

SpecialCase.ToTitle.d: ToTitle maps the rune to title case giving priority to the special mapping.

SpecialCase.ToUpper.d: ToUpper maps the rune to upper case giving priority to the special mapping.

TitleCase.d: Indices into the Delta arrays inside CaseRanges for case mapping.

To.s: func To(_case int, r rune) rune
To.d: To maps the rune to the specified case: UpperCase, LowerCase, or TitleCase.

ToLower.d: ToLower maps the rune to lower case.

ToTitle.d: ToTitle maps the rune to title case.

ToUpper.d: ToUpper maps the rune to upper case.

UpperCase.d: Indices into the Delta arrays inside CaseRanges for case mapping.

UpperLower.d: If the Delta field of a CaseRange is UpperLower, it means this CaseRange represents a sequence of the form (say) Upper Lower Upper Lower.

Version.d: Version is the Unicode edition from which the tables are derived.

AppendRune.d: AppendRune appends the UTF-8 encoding of r to the end of p and returns the extended buffer.

DecodeLastRune.d: DecodeLastRune unpacks the last UTF-8 encoding in p and returns the rune and its width in bytes.

DecodeLastRuneInString.s: func DecodeLastRuneInString(s string) (r rune, size int)
DecodeLastRuneInString.d: DecodeLastRuneInString is like DecodeLastRune but its input is a string.

DecodeRune.d: DecodeRune unpacks the first UTF-8 encoding in p and returns the rune and its width in bytes.

DecodeRuneInString.s: func DecodeRuneInString(s string) (r rune, size int)
DecodeRuneInString.d: DecodeRuneInString is like DecodeRune but its input is a string.

EncodeRune.d: EncodeRune writes into p (which must be large enough) the UTF-8 encoding of the rune.

FullRune.d: FullRune reports whether the bytes in p begin with a full UTF-8 encoding of a rune.

FullRuneInString.d: FullRuneInString is like FullRune but its input is a string.

RuneCount.d: RuneCount returns the number of runes in p.

RuneCountInString.d: RuneCountInString is like RuneCount but its input is a string.

RuneLen.d: RuneLen returns the number of bytes in the UTF-8 encoding of the rune.

RuneStart.d: RuneStart reports whether the byte could be the first byte of an encoded, possibly invalid rune.

Valid.d: Valid reports whether p consists entirely of valid UTF-8-encoded runes.

ValidRune.d: ValidRune reports whether r can be legally encoded as UTF-8.

ValidString.d: ValidString reports whether s consists entirely of valid UTF-8-encoded runes.
